Lexikon der indogermanischen Verben
The
Lexikon der indogermanischen Verben
(
LIV
,
'
lexicon of Indo-European verbs
'
) is an
etymological dictionary
of the
Proto-Indo-European
(PIE) verb. The first edition appeared in 1998, edited by
Helmut Rix
. A second edition followed in 2001. The book may be seen as an update to the verb entries of the
Indogermanisches etymologisches Wörterbuch
(
IEW
) by
Julius Pokorny
. It was the first dictionary fully utilizing the modern three-
laryngeal theory
with reconstructions of Indo-European verbal roots.
The
LIV'
s hypothesis about aspect
The authors of the
LIV
assume a dichotomy between
telic
verbs (terminated: for example,
*
leh₂p-
'to light up') and
atelic
verbs (ongoing: for example,
*
bʰeh₂-
'to shine') in early stages of Proto-Indo-European. Before the
daughter languages
split off,
aspect
emerged as a new grammatical category.
Telic verbs were interpreted as
aorist
forms, and the missing
present
was formed with various suffixes (for example,
*
leh₂p-
:
*
l̥h₂p-
sḱé
-
) and the
nasal infix
(
*
l̥h₂-
né
-p-
), all of which are supposed to come from old grammatical forms of uncertain meaning.
Atelic verbs were interpreted as present forms, and the missing aorist was formed with the suffix
-s-
, yielding the
sigmatic
aorist.
